I'm deciding to keep the shared quality module returning raw data and kinds, leaving the actual copy/formatting strings to the renderer's COPY object, then starting to write `quality.ts` with its type imports.

I'm defining a `BandComparison` type with insufficient/same/higher-band kinds, and writing `compareBands` to round both accuracies first before diffing, so the comparison sentence matches the rounded percentages shown elsewhere. I'm also flagging that I need to double-check whether `BandBars` displays raw or rounded accuracy, since if it's unrounded the percentages could show decimals inconsistently — something to verify against `report.ts` shortly.

Now I'm sketching out the data shapes for the overall comparison view: a `GameComparisonRow` capturing per-game index, players, result, inclusion status, accuracy (or 'insufficient'/null for excluded or legacy games), and blunder counts; an `OverallQualityView` bundling the settled/elevated bands, comparison, totals, excluded count, rows, and a legacy flag — which I'm reconsidering to compute based on whether any included game lacks a summary rather than just checking `report.totals`. I'm also defining a `GameQualityView` union for individual games (excluded/legacy/ok), with the 'ok' case including the game, summary, side, a timeline span, comparison, and a list of loss rows with move index, label, centipawn loss, blunder flag, and time spent.

For computing the time span, I'm aligning start/end microsecond timestamps to the timeline's start and formatting the elapsed time between them, only when properly aligned. For loss labels, I'm looking up the matching timeline move by game and move index to get the SAN notation, falling back to a move-number-only label if the move can't be found. I'm also determining which side the player was on — white, black, or both if all moves were made by them.

Now I'm moving into the `MoveQuality.tsx` renderer component, setting up state for the selected tab (either 'overall' or a specific game index) and planning tabs for the overall view plus one per game, including excluded games which will show a note explaining why they were excluded from accuracy calculations.

I'm handling keyboard navigation for the tabs — arrow keys, Home, and End move focus with automatic selection using roving tabindex and ref arrays. For the overall panel I'm laying out two columns: the left side holds the band bars showing accuracy by pulse range, though I need to verify the copy matches the contract exactly (titles, notes, and labels about minimum scored moves per range) against what the tests expect. The right side will have a session facts list covering scored moves, blunders, elevated pulse moves, and games included/excluded, organized under headings like "Scoring coverage" and "Blunders," followed by a comparison sentence summarizing what this data supports.

Below that, I'm planning a game comparison list where each row is a clickable button showing the game number, players, result, accuracy (or a note if insufficient/excluded), and blunder count, opening the corresponding tab. For the individual game panel, the left column will show a summary (result, ending, side played, time control, session span) plus accuracy stats (overall, settled, elevated, scored moves, blunders, think time), followed by a list of the largest locally scored changes with centipawn loss, blunder tags, and a button to jump to the timeline that's disabled with a reason if no timestamp exists.

Now I'm working out the "Open on timeline" wiring — a callback that passes the timestamp up to App, which needs new state to track the focused timeline moment. I need to be careful here: since the Timeline component persists across session changes, I have to guard against stale focus state carrying over into a new session, so I'm including the session ID in the focus object so it only applies when it matches the current session.

Similarly, I need to prevent the effect from re-triggering an unwanted jump if the user navigates away and back to the same session — I'll use a ref to track the already-applied sequence so the mount doesn't reapply an old focus.

Finally, I'm checking the rounding behavior in BandBars for accuracy display and verifying the elevated-state test assertions.
